name: talaria-v0-2-block-markdown
description: v0.2 block-level markdown + transcript differentiation (plan revision 2, post doc-review): ADR-first bounded-rendering claim (four ceilings, descendant-counted), domain terminal-path commits under a typed cause with exact content preservation, safe parser+rendering boundary, hybrid pane with two live tails, kind channels, restated two-part gate proof with a sideband timeline, re-run green. Every build unit is cross-reviewed by the Codex engine before its dependents run, and dependents consume the review VERDICT, not its completion: a review returning findings blocks its dependents until the findings are fixed and re-reviewed. U4-U6 commit to the branch feat/v0-2-block-markdown-build (KTD8 branch-hold), merged to main only after U6's gate runs green and CR6 passes; U1-U3 merge independently.

units.label: ADR-0006: the block-aware bounded-rendering claim
units.prompt: U1: Write ADR-0006 recording the block-aware bounded-rendering claim BEFORE any widget work: the FOUR ceilings of KTD1 with their exact measurement points - (a) TWO-TIER descendant count (a table mounts one widget per cell, so top-level blocks bound nothing): the folded window (everything except the newest entry and live tails) <= 600 descendants, AND a TWO-CONDITION per-entry trigger on the newest entry and each tail - descendants (or pre-parse token estimate) > 1,200 (the 1,000-row table measures 1,003, fitting with headroom) OR projected line span > mount_cap (500) lines (a 10,000-line open fence is ONE block with two descendants standing 10,004 rows tall - probed - so descendants alone cannot see it) - beyond which THAT ENTRY ALONE falls back to line rendering with a banner note; a line-rendered entry folds under today's line cap (desired_top may land inside it), so the fallback can never exceed the line machinery's own bounds - observed at every 50ms coalescing boundary via Textual's own tree, with the recorded reason why 'every instant' is not the enforcement point (Markdown.update parses off the pump and mounts in batches of 200, transiently holding old and new blocks); (b) rendered height bounded by the same two tiers; (c) reconcile work measured as PARSER-INPUT BYTES per boundary (the reparse window from the last unfinished top-level block - probed: constant 500-byte appends into an open fence produce growing parser inputs 499/999/1,499/..., so bytes-handed-to-append understates work), proportional to unfinished block + new bytes with the latency ceiling as the enforceable bound and the per-entry fallback as the relief valve; (d) p99 apply latency under 50ms on the exact workloads (unclosed fence fed 100 lines/boundary to 10,000 lines; table fed 10 rows/boundary to 1,000 rows; time.monotonic around TranscriptPane.apply; first 10 boundaries warm-up-excluded). Amend ADR-0005 decision 3 (the 500-line-widget 'at every instant' cap): 500 stays DEFAULT_MOUNT_CAP - the line cap for line-rendered surfaces and the per-entry line-span trigger - while 600 is the folded-window descendant ceiling the gate enforces; state the two-tier model in those terms AND decision 7 (literal_text-only - untrusted text may additionally reach the screen through the KTD4-configured parser and rendering hooks and nothing else). Record requirements amendments RA1 (underscore emphasis + strikethrough in scope) and RA2 (R3 met by cell wrapping, not cell focus) and the KTD8 fallback trigger with its branch-hold mechanism. Mirror to docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md. Read docs/plans/2026-08-09-talaria-v0-2-block-markdown-plan.md (unit U1, KTD1/KTD8, RA1/RA2, R13) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: Domain: terminal-path commits, exact preservation, entry-scoped projection
units.prompt: U2: In the domain plus the transport cause seam (ADR-0002: the domain imports no framework), do four things. (1) Typed terminal cause: the transport's four disconnect sites (talaria/transport/source.py:383 credential failure, :404 failed dial, :445 orderly close, :708 exhausted reconnect) feed a typed end-of-stream cause; terminal causes (auth_failed, dial_failed, orderly_close, reconnect_exhausted, operator teardown) and _on_error (talaria/domain/state.py:1586 - NOT :1181, that citation was stale) commit partial streaming AND reasoning buffers as entries before clearing; a transient reconnect resuming the same response commits nothing and never duplicates (the segment/interim machinery is the dedupe backstop, pinned). cancel_turn ALREADY commits both buffers (state.py:580-585) - the COMMIT behavior is pinned by regression, and its ONE change is that the preservation work removes its stripping (the .strip() at :580 and .lstrip() at :583). (2) Exact content preservation: content-channel strings are preserved exactly (coerce_text's stripping at talaria/domain/normalize.py:224 stays for diagnostics only; the interim path state.py:1435, the final-body left-strip :1510, and cancel_turn's strips stop mutating content) - leading indentation survives byte-for-byte (fixture: FOUR-space indentation committing as an indented code block - gfm parses two-space indentation as a paragraph), trailing blank lines, whitespace-only bodies, and open fences survive across interim, final-replacement, error, cancellation, and disconnect, each pinned. WIRING: the typed cause travels the live path end-to-end - LiveSource.bind to note_connection_state (talaria/ui/app.py:1455-1467, wired at talaria/cli.py:453) to the domain transition - so this unit owns those two wiring files (the wiring lines only; U4 edits app.py later and the units are sequential) and an end-to-end live-source test. (3) Entry-scoped projection: TranscriptView grows per-entry records (stable monotonic entry id stable under condensation, kind, raw body, committed flag, line span) plus TWO provisional tails (assistant and reasoning, each with raw text and a stream generation counter that increments on message.interim or any replace-wins path) - today projection.py:276 projects only the assistant buffer; R18's projection half lands here. message.interim respects the committed/interim boundary and bumps the generation. A cancellation mid-table (after the header row) commits the partial table (R14's mid-table leg). (4) The reasoning weld stays decoration on line-rendered surfaces only; the flattened decorated line buffer stays byte-identical for terminal_read and content_is_complete - tests/domain/test_projection.py::test_every_transcript_entry_survives_into_the_line_buffer must pass UNMODIFIED. Note: the stress corpus's projected counts change when error paths commit partials; the re-baseline is U6's, not yours. Read docs/plans/2026-08-09-talaria-v0-2-block-markdown-plan.md (unit U2, KTD6/KTD7, R6/R14/R16/R18) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: The block factory and its forgery proof
units.prompt: U3: Create talaria/ui/blocks.py - the single constructor for safely configured Markdown entry documents. Parser side: parser_factory returning MarkdownIt('gfm-like') with html=False and linkify=False, open_links=False, defang before parse at parity with talaria/ui/literal.py, and an ALLOWLIST PIN: a snapshot test of the parser's exact enabled rule set (RA1's underscore emphasis and strikethrough are in it; any preset drift or new rule fails the pin). Rendering side (the parser config is NOT the whole boundary): Textual installs @click action metadata for links unconditionally (_markdown.py:342) and emits Markdown.LinkClicked regardless of open_links (:1194), and renders images as alt text with the target dropped (:346) - so the factory's document subclass renders links styled but with NO action metadata (test: clicking emits no LinkClicked and opens/fetches nothing) and renders images as 'alt (target)' text per R10. Prove every forbidden channel: HTML literalized visible (never dropped), Rich console markup unparsed, ANSI defanged, bare URLs stay text, entry isolation across an unclosed fence (R15), and the Textual 8.2.8 pin test - append reparses from the last unfinished block, update replaces, and the public Markdown.get_stream (:1155) exists (the corrected KTD3 evidence) - failing loudly on upgrade drift. R4 scope note: configuration and subclassed rendering hooks only; no parser or block-assembly engine. Read docs/plans/2026-08-09-talaria-v0-2-block-markdown-plan.md (unit U3, KTD3/KTD4, RA1, R4/R9/R10/R15) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: The hybrid transcript pane
units.prompt: U4: Rebuild TranscriptPane as the hybrid, committing to the feat/v0-2-block-markdown-build branch (KTD8 branch-hold). Committed assistant/reasoning entries mount one Markdown document each (built by talaria/ui/blocks.py), every other kind keeps one TranscriptLine per line, and the in-flight streams render in TWO independently keyed live tail documents (assistant and reasoning can stream in the same turn - R18) driven by public Markdown.append at the 50ms boundary using the projection's stream generation: same generation appends the suffix beyond what was last applied, changed generation calls update() with the authoritative text - NEVER a prefix guess. Commit hands each tail's source to its entry document keyed by entry id, no pane rebuild. Restate rendered_lines as a content reconstruction (line widgets contribute their line; block entries contribute their projected source lines via line spans) so pane.rendered_lines == view.lines[condensed_count:] stays true, and update the three existing suites that assert it IN PLACE (tests/ui/test_markdown.py:297, tests/transport/test_session_startup.py:607, tests/transport/test_source_equivalence.py:277+299) - never delete them. Condensation over mixed units: desired_top computed in lines, rounds UP to the next unit boundary, except the newest entry is always mounted whole with overage recorded (KTD2's rule); banner line arithmetic still sums. Enforce KTD1(a)'s TWO-TIER ceilings at every coalescing boundary: folded window <= 600 descendants; newest entry and each tail under the TWO-CONDITION trigger (descendants/estimate > 1,200 OR line span > mount_cap 500 lines - the 10,000-line fence is one block, two descendants, 10,004 rows: only the span condition sees it), beyond which THAT entry alone line-renders with a banner note and folds under today's line cap like any line content (the fallback also ends the growing reparse of an ever-open block). ZERO-BLOCK sources (empty/whitespace-only/newline-only - they mount height-zero documents, probed) never take the block path: they line-render, preserving blank rows as visible line widgets. R16 clauses 2-3: a terminal path stops and awaits pending widget writes; a stale stream write after its widget was condensed away or removed updates nothing and raises nothing. Retire the inline styler from the live path (MARKDOWN_KINDS moves to blocks; talaria/ui/markdown.py is retained as the KTD8 fallback's styling half with a comment saying why; its pane-level assertions move to the reconstruction). Per-construct render oracles: heading, bullet list, ordered list, block quote, fence, table each asserted by block class and geometry and each proven to fail when flattened (R1). Tables per RA2's exact column arithmetic (wrapping alone starves columns under grid-columns:auto, probed [0,0,58,1,1] at 80 cols): for N columns in content width W, available A = W - (3N + 1); CAP = max(8, floor(A/N)); m_i = min(longest_word_i, CAP); if sum(m_i) <= A give each column m_i plus proportional remainder, else give every column floor(A/N) with a hard floor of 3 and character-wrap longer words; the factory's table subclass sets these widths explicitly. Assert the ACTUAL PAINTED CONTENT of every cell at 80 columns, the five-column probe case included. Reader anchor and follow-bottom survive reinterpretation, resize, condensation (R17). Read docs/plans/2026-08-09-talaria-v0-2-block-markdown-plan.md (unit U4, KTD1/KTD2/KTD3, RA2, R1/R2/R3/R5/R16/R17/R18) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: The restated gate, the sideband timeline, and the green re-run
units.prompt:
U6: On the feat/v0-2-block-markdown-build branch (KTD8 branch-hold), replace interface_shows_everything's one-line-one-widget claim with the TWO-PART ownership proof: (1) mounted-window ownership - every projected line inside the mounted window of a block entry is covered by that entry's document blocks' source_range spans, with the blank-line accounting rule stated explicitly (probed fact: 'a

# h
' yields ranges (0,1) and (2,3) with the blank line owned by neither block; the proof accounts inter-block blanks to the entry's span), and the proof applies to BOTH provisional tail documents at every checkpoint, not only committed entries; ZERO-BLOCK sources line-render (a zero-block document mounts at HEIGHT ZERO - probed - so widget presence is not visibility; empty/whitespace/newline-only entries render as line widgets preserving their blank rows) and fall under the existing window comparison, not the block proof; (2) condensed-range accounting - folded units accounted by line spans in the banner arithmetic. Add the semantic comparison (defanged source vs rendered content per construct) and MUTATION TESTS: dropped text, a wrong block class, and a hidden construct must each make the gate fail. Per-construct oracles for every R1 construct, each proven to fail when flattened. R11a GUARD: content_is_complete (gate.py:290) and its callers are untouched - the diff must not touch the function and the v0.1 projection pin passes verbatim. Confirmed-cancel and terminal disconnect are NOT wire frames (interrupt replies decode to NonEventFrame ignored at state.py:1246; transport callbacks are unrecorded) - build the deterministic SIDEBAND TIMELINE: a scripted action track (timestamped confirmed-cancel and typed-disconnect injections ordered against frame indices) the replay source applies alongside the frame log; determinism includes the sideband; scope is exactly these two action kinds, nothing richer. Grow the feature corpus (every construct, early termination by cancel/error/typed-disconnect INCLUDING the mid-table case, parser attacks, kind groups, 80-column resize, the KTD1(d) workloads at their exact sizes); assert progressiveness at timed checkpoints including the two-tail overlap case (R18); replay determinism on normalized block structure under pinned width/theme/framework, sideband included; re-run the gate green over existing AND feature corpora (the U2 re-baseline of the stress corpus lands here); record the verdict in docs/analysis/2026-08-09-block-markdown-gate-results.md pinning theme textual-dark, exact terminal sizes including 80 columns, Textual 8.2.8, corpus identities by sha256, and reproduction commands. Read docs/plans/2026-08-09-talaria-v0-2-block-markdown-plan.md (unit U6, KTD1/KTD8, R5/R11b/R12/R13/R14/R18 with the R11a guard; AE6) as your authoritative spec.
